title: Support of a relative cycle along a smooth morphism of relative dimension r is open and closed

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Compare the coefficient of the unique irreducible component through each point of the fibre, show the coefficient is unchanged by any base change of locally Noetherian schemes because the smooth component pulls back to a reduced scheme whose irreducible components carry the same coefficient by the definition of base change in the relative fields section, reduce local constancy to checking specializations and realize each specialization by a discrete valuation ring mapping into X via the Properties lemma, pull the situation back so the valuation ring maps to the base with a section, use the connected-components machinery of More on Morphisms and the section lemma to shrink X so the fibres are connected, observe smooth connected fibres are irreducible so the generic fibre is a multiple of the whole fibre, and conclude by the defining specialization relation of relative cycles that the closed fibre carries the same coefficient (source lines 1257-1303)

standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the morphism S' to X mapping the generic point to x' and the closed point to x, turning the specialization check into a valuation-ring computation.

standard_prerequisites.use: After replacing X by an open subscheme the fibres of X to S are connected, using the section sigma of the base-changed family.

core_obligations: Show that for f : X to S smooth of relative dimension r with S locally Noetherian and alpha a relative r-cycle, the support of alpha is open and closed in X, by showing the function x mapping to the coefficient n_x of the unique irreducible component Z(x) of X_s through x is locally constant (proof lines 1257-1262). First, prove base-change invariance: for any morphism g : S' to S of locally Noetherian schemes with base changes X' and alpha' = g^*alpha, and x' over x, the component Z(x) is smooth over kappa(s) so its base change to kappa(s') is reduced, Z(x') is an irreducible component of that scheme, and by the definition of base change in section-relative-fields (tag 0H4E) the coefficient of Z(x') in alpha'_{s'} equals the coefficient of Z(x) in alpha_s (proof lines 1264-1276). Second, since X is locally Noetherian, local constancy of x mapping to n_x reduces to equality along specializations x' leading to x; realize the specialization by a morphism from the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring S' to X sending eta to x' and 0 to x (properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-specialization-dvr, tag 054F); base changing f by S' to S gives a family with a section sigma : S' to X' such that sigma(eta) specializes to sigma(0) over the given specialization, reducing to the DVR case (proof lines 1278-1289). Third, for S the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with a section sigma : S to X, apply the connected-components discussion of more-morphisms-section-connected-components (tag 055K) and especially more-morphisms-lemma-connected-along-section-open (tag 055R) to shrink X so its fibres over S are connected; smooth connected fibres are irreducible, so alpha_eta = n[X_eta] with n = n_{sigma(eta)}, and the specialization relation sp_{X/S}(alpha_eta) = alpha_0 forces alpha_0 = n[X_0], i.e. n_{sigma(0)} = n (proof lines 1291-1302).
proof_roadmap: Setup: parametrize the support by the coefficient n_x of the unique irreducible component of the fibre through x (proof lines 1257-1262).
Base-change invariance of the coefficient via reducedness of the pulled-back smooth component and the definition of base change over fields (proof lines 1264-1276).
Reduce local constancy to specializations and realize them by a valuation ring mapping into X, then base change to get a sectioned family (proof lines 1278-1289).

DVR case: shrink so fibres are connected using the section lemma, note smooth connected fibres are irreducible, and conclude equal coefficients from the specialization relation (proof lines 1291-1302).
